title: Register halving loop count
statement: Let $A$ be a register program with state set $Lambda$, let $oracle$ be an oracle, and let $y$ be an input bit string. Choose distinct registers $t$ and $c$ and states $test$, $halve$, $bump$, and $done$, such that the instructions at these states respectively test whether register $t$ is zero (proceeding to $done$ if so and otherwise to $halve$), replace $t$ by $floor(t/2)$ and proceed to $bump$, and increment $c$ and return to $test$. If all registers initially have values at most $B$ and the initial value of $c$ plus the binary length of the initial value of $t$ is at most $B$, then the program reaches $done$ with $t=0$ and $c$ equal to its initial value plus that binary length; every configuration before reaching $done$ satisfies the execution guard for bound $B$.
hypotheses_covered: A register program $A$ with state set $Lambda$
An oracle and input bit string $y$
States test, halve, bump, and done with the specified instructions
Initial register valuation $v$ with every register at most $B$
Initial value of $c$ plus binary length of initial value of $t$ is at most $B$
